title: Anthropic Launched Mods for Claude Code. Let's Build a Tiny One in TypeScript.
content: Anthropic just made Claude Code rewriteable from the inside. Not with a config flag. With TypeScript. On October 3, 2026, Anthropic introduced Mods for Claude Code : small TypeScript functions that hook into events inside the tool. A mod can rewrite a prompt, block or retry a tool call, approve or deny a permission, redact secrets from tool output, or change what you see in the UI. Hooks already existed. Anthropic is clear about the gap: "Hooks helped give users some of this control, but hooks can't rewrite events, draw new UI, or replace features. Mods can." That distinction matters. Hooks watch. Mods rewrite. And here is the part I keep thinking about. Mods are not sandboxed. They run with the same access as Claude Code itself. Anthropic ships a built-in sec-default mod that loads first on Team and Enterprise plans, so user-installed mods cannot override your permission deny rules. So let's build a tiny version of that idea. By the end, you'll run one command: npx tsx mods.ts And wat
author: Bobby Hall Jr
summary_zh: 文章介绍了 Anthropic 于 2026 年 10 月 3 日为 Claude Code 推出的 Mods 功能。Mods 是挂在 Claude Code 内部事件上的小型 TypeScript 函数，可以改写提示词、拦截或重试工具调用、批准或拒绝权限请求、从工具输出中隐去密钥，还能修改 UI。文章讲清了 Mods 和原有 Hooks 的区别（Hooks 只能观察，Mods 可以改写事件和替换功能），提醒 Mods 不在沙箱中运行、拥有与 Claude Code 相同的权限，并带读者用 TypeScript 写一个简单的 Mod。
pin_reason: Mods 是 Claude Code 扩展方式的一次重大升级，本文是较早的上手教程，并点明了它与 Hooks 的区别和安全风险，适合长期参考。

title: Does a Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook keep a blocked prompt out of the transcript? 6 of 6 never reached the model, all 6 were still written to it
content: 6 of 6 prompts that a UserPromptSubmit hook blocked never reached the model, yet all 6 were still written to the session transcript (4 of them twice), and claude -p exited 0 with "subtype": "success" every time. Context injection matched the hooks page: plain stdout and additionalContext arrived in 2 of 2 runs each, 10,000 characters arrived whole, 50,000 became a 1,949-character preview, and a hook that exited 1 or printed a bare JSON object delivered nothing in 4 of 4 runs. UserPromptSubmit runs after you press Enter and before Claude sees what you typed. That position makes it the hook people reach for in two situations: adding context to every prompt (the current branch, today's date, a rule worth repeating) and refusing a prompt outright (a pasted key, a request that should never go out). Both jobs come down to one question. Of everything the hook prints, what goes in front of the model, what goes to the person or the script running Claude Code, and what goes to disk? The hooks re
author: Rulestack
summary_zh: 作者对 Claude Code 的 UserPromptSubmit hook 做了实测：被 hook 拦截的 6 条 prompt 都没有发给模型，但 6 条全部写进了会话 transcript，其中 4 条还写了两次，而且 claude -p 每次都以 exit 0、subtype success 退出。上下文注入的表现和官方文档一致：纯 stdout 和 additionalContext 都能送达；1 万字符能完整送达，5 万字符只剩 1949 字符的预览；hook 以 exit 1 退出或只输出一个裸 JSON 对象时，什么都不会注入。这篇文章提醒大家，拦截 prompt 并不会把敏感信息挡在本地日志之外，对用 hook 防止密钥泄露的人很有参考价值。

title: Claude Code MCP: Connected but Not Working? Check These Three Gates
content: An MCP server can appear in claude mcp list and still fail the first real request. In most cases the connection is fine and one of three separate gates is closed. Checking them in order saves a lot of configuration churn. The three gates Every MCP request from Claude Code passes three independent checks: Gate Question it answers Who controls it 1. Project-server approval May Claude Code load this connection in this project? You, in an interactive session, plus any organisation restrictions 2. Tool permission May Claude call this specific tool now? Claude Code permission rules in personal, project and organisation settings 3. Data access Does the credential behind the server allow this read or write? The external system, for example GitHub, using the token's permissions Passing one gate says nothing about the next. Approving a tool call in Claude Code cannot grant a repository permission your token lacks, and a token with full access does not help if the project server was never approve
author: Poorna Reddy
summary_zh: 文章针对 Claude Code 中 MCP 服务器在 claude mcp list 中显示已连接、实际请求却失败的常见问题，提出了按顺序排查三道独立“关卡”的方法。这三道关卡分别是项目级服务器审批、工具权限规则（个人/项目/组织设置）和外部系统凭证的数据访问权限。按顺序逐一检查可以快速定位问题，避免反复修改配置。

title: 5 Reasons Claude Code Seems to Ignore Your CLAUDE.md
content: When Claude Code skips a rule you wrote in CLAUDE.md , the file is rarely broken. Usually the rule never loaded, lost to a conflicting rule, or was never something a context file could enforce. These are the five causes to check, in order. 1. The session started in the wrong directory Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md from the directory where the session starts and from every parent directory. A file in a sibling package does not apply just because it exists in the repository. Start in services/billing/ and the billing guidance is relevant. Start in apps/web/ and it is not. 2. The nested file has not loaded yet Files below the working directory are not loaded at startup. They load when Claude reads files in that directory. If you start at the repository root and ask a question before Claude has opened anything in apps/web/ , the web guidance is not in context yet. Run /context to see which memory files Claude Code reports as loaded. 3. Two files disagree Loaded files are
author: Poorna Reddy
summary_zh: 文章排查 Claude Code 似乎忽略 CLAUDE.md 规则的五个常见原因：多数时候不是文件写错了，而是规则根本没有加载、被与之冲突的规则覆盖，或者这类要求本来就不是上下文文件能强制执行的。文章还说明了加载机制：会话启动目录及其所有上级目录中的 CLAUDE.md 会被加载；工作目录下层的 CLAUDE.md 不会在启动时加载，要等 Claude 读取该目录中的文件时才加载。整篇是一份按顺序检查的实用清单。

title: 想知道 Claude Code 額度被哪個專案吃掉，就寫了個小工具
content:
撞到 Claude Code 5 小時或每週上限的時候，我最想知道的是哪個專案用掉的，但 /usage 答不出來。它只給帳號層級的百分比，再加幾個像「>150k context」、「4+ parallel sessions」的標籤，沒有拆到專案，那些百分比也沒辦法自己驗算。 Claude Code 本來就會把每則訊息的 token 用量寫進本機的 session transcript（ ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl ）。所以我寫了一個 skill 叫 quota-audit，讀這些檔案，按專案、按 skill 整理用量，也列出真正撞到上限的時間點和當下被擋的 repo。它只讀檔，不會寫入任何東西，資料也不會送出去。 報表長怎樣 開頭先放幾行算好的結論，接著每個視窗（5h、24h、7d）一列總覽，最後才是最長那個視窗的明細。節錄一段範例： KEY FINDINGS (7d window)
  • Estimated cost $147.31, 65% of it in my-app ($95.20)
  • Top skill is ai-work at 54%
  • 11 sessions crossed 150k context, $88.40 combined (60% of window cost)
  • 3 rate-limit hits in 7d; 14 all-time, most often blocking my-app (9 times)

window     est. cost  sessions   >150k   hits   top project
5h            $12.40         5       2      0   my-app 81%
24h           $38.75        21       4      1   my-app 70%
7d           $147.31        99      11      3   my-app 65% skill 是逐則訊息歸因的，不是只看 session 用哪個指令開頭，所以具名 skill 跟一般互動的切分比較可信。超過 150k context 的 session 會直接列出名字，依花費由高到低排，這通常
author: Rosehsu
summary_zh: 作者开发了 quota-audit skill，读取 Claude Code 写在本机的 session transcript（~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl），按项目和 skill 拆分 token 用量与估算成本。它弥补了 /usage 只给账号层级百分比的不足，能找出真正撞到 5 小时或每周上限的时间点和当时被挡的 repo，还能统计超过 150k context 的会话造成了多少成本。工具只读本地文件，不写入也不上传数据，适合想弄清额度花在哪里的重度用户。

title: DeReAct: Decomposed Reasoning and Acting for Reliable AI Agents
content:
arXiv:2610.02351v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: ReAct-based agents typically rely on a single LLM policy to propose actions, interact with the environment, and decide when a task is complete. This coupling makes action authorization and completion control difficult to enforce independently, allowing errors to propagate and unsupported completion claims to terminate execution. We introduce DeReAct, a modular agent architecture that externalizes two gating policies: a Critic that validates proposed actions before execution, and a Context Manager that reconstructs an environment-supported \textsc{State} and certifies task completion.
  Across GAIA and SWE-bench Verified, DeReAct improves Pass@1 most for weaker Brain models, with gains of 6.5--7.0 points for Qwen3-Coder-480B and 4.2--5.2 points for Claude Sonnet~4.5; gains diminish as Brain capability increases. Trajectory and ablation analyses show that external gating is effective when targeted failures are sufficiently prevalent and th
author: Ajay Vohra, Tao Chen, Neeti Narayan, Caron Zhang
summary_zh: 论文提出 DeReAct 模块化智能体架构，把 ReAct 中由单一 LLM 同时负责的动作授权和任务完成判定拆分出来，由两个独立的门控策略负责：Critic 在动作执行前做校验，Context Manager 重建有环境依据的状态并认证任务是否完成。在 GAIA 和 SWE-bench Verified 上，较弱的 Brain 模型提升最明显，例如 Qwen3-Coder-480B 的 Pass@1 提升 6.5–7.0 分。这对设计可靠的 AI 编程智能体工作流有参考价值，尤其适合用来防止错误传播和缺乏依据的「已完成」声明。

title: Claude Opus Price 2026: Opus 5.5 Wins at $4 vs Opus 5
content: The Claude Opus price dropped for the first time in the model line's history: Claude Opus 5.5 bills at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, against $5 and $25 for Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 ( Anthropic ; pricing docs ). Verdict: Opus 5.5 wins Opus-tier API work as of September 2026 — it undercuts the model it replaces and beats the $10/$50 Fable 5.1 on Anthropic's published benchmarks, while Sonnet 5 at $2/$10 ( pricing docs ) still wins high-volume classification where Opus capability is wasted. TL;DR Opus 5.5 (released 22 September 2026): $4 in, $20 out per million, 20% below Opus 5 ( Anthropic ). Cache reads fell 60% to $0.20 per million — the lever that moves real agent bills ( Anthropic ). Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 remain at $5 in, $25 out — the rate every Opus has carried since Opus 4.5 ( Anthropic ). A typical workload runs 40% cheaper end-to-end: fewer tokens per task, cheaper tokens ( Anthropic ). Fable 5.1 at $10/$50 loses its case for cost-conscious teams; Sonne
author: Shaam
summary_zh: 文章对比了 Claude Opus 系列的 API 定价：Opus 5.5 于 2026 年 9 月 22 日发布，价格为每百万输入 token 4 美元、输出 token 20 美元，是 Opus 系列首次降价，比 Opus 5 和 Opus 4.8 便宜 20%。缓存读取价格也降低 60%，至每百万 token 0.2 美元，对重度使用 Agent 的场景省钱效果最大。作者认为 Opus 级任务应优先选 Opus 5.5，高并发分类等简单任务用 Sonnet 5（2/10 美元）更划算。

title: llama-server's logprobs are placeholders when speculative decoding is on
content: TL;DR : When llama-server runs with speculative decoding (a draft model with -md , MTP, or one of the n-gram types), every token that comes out of the speculative loop is sent with logprob: 0.0 and an empty top_logprobs list. The code sets the probability to 1.0 with the comment // set later and never sets it. With a draft model that is every token after the first. On b11430, the current release, the mean logprob of 64-token samples at temperature 1 was -0.48 without speculation and -0.0011 with it. The generated text looked normal, and nothing in the response or the log says the numbers are fill-ins. There is no per-request switch: the request fields that used to tune speculation are compiled out and ignored. Send logprob requests to an instance started without speculation. The tokens themselves are fine: on a small fixture, the server's speculative output had the same next-token distribution as plain sampling. The llama-speculative example program did not. The toolkit's check-spec-lo
author: The Homelab Postmortem
summary_zh: 文章发现 llama-server 开启推测解码（草稿模型、MTP 或 n-gram）后，推测循环输出的 token 的 logprob 都被硬编码为 0.0，top_logprobs 为空。源码中标注“set later”，但这个值后来一直没有被填上。作者在 b11430 版本上实测，开启后平均 logprob 从 -0.48 变成 -0.0011，响应和日志里都没有任何提示。作者建议把需要 logprobs 的请求发到未开启推测解码的实例。

title: Como funciona a memória de um agente de IA (e o que acontece quando ela esquece do jeito errado)
content: Um modelo de linguagem não lembra de nada. Cada chamada recebe um prompt, gera uma resposta e pronto, esqueceu. Quando um agente "lembra" que o projeto usa pytest , quem lembrou foi um sistema fora do modelo, que guardou isso em algum lugar e recolocou no prompt na hora certa. Esse sistema é a memória do agente. Nesse post eu explico como ela funciona, mostro quatro políticas de memória que implementei e conto o que aconteceu quando coloquei as quatro pra acompanhar o mesmo projeto simulado por meses. Parte 1: como funciona a memória de um agente Por que não mandar a conversa inteira no prompt O jeito mais simples seria mandar o histórico todo em toda chamada. Funciona por um tempo. O problema é que o histórico só cresce: uma hora não cabe mais, e bem antes disso o consumo de tokens corresponde a informações que podem não agregar em nada no verdadeiro intuito do prompt. E tem um problema pior: o histórico mistura informação velha e nova sem dizer qual vale. Se o serviço mudou de região
author: Matheus Persch
summary_zh: 文章用葡萄牙语讲解AI智能体的记忆机制：模型本身没有记忆，由外部系统负责存储信息，并在合适的时候重新注入提示词。作者实现了四种记忆策略，让它们跟踪同一个模拟项目长达数月，对比各自的表现，重点分析遗忘方式不当带来的问题。这些结论可以帮助理解CLAUDE.md这类持久化上下文的设计思路。

title: When you "repair" truncated JSON, you stop noticing it was truncated
content: Disclosure: I wrote this article together with an AI assistant (Claude). The AI wrote and ran all the code below and checked the results. I'm not a professional programmer, so please read it with that in mind. LLM APIs return HTTP 200 even when the output stops because it hit the token limit. Nothing looks like an error, so a JSON reply that was cut off halfway can sail straight into the next step of your pipeline. A common fix is to put a repair library such as json-repair in front of the parser. It closes the brackets you were missing and hands you valid JSON, which is very handy. But when the JSON was cut off, "repairing" it also hides the fact that it was cut off. That's obvious in hindsight, but I had no idea how often it actually bites, so I tried every possible cut and counted. Here's the short version: Passed through a repair library, almost everything (98.5%) came back as plausible-looking JSON Even with a JSON Schema where every field is required, 137 of 853 truncations (16.1
author: ToNBi
summary_zh: 文章指出：LLM API 因 token 上限截断输出时仍然返回 HTTP 200，而用 json-repair 之类的库去“修复”被截断的 JSON，会把截断这件事一并掩盖，残缺数据就会悄悄流进下游流程。作者在 Claude 的协助下，对所有可能的截断位置逐一做了实验，统计出这个问题实际出现的频率。文章提醒在 LLM 结构化输出流程里，应先检查 stop_reason/finish_reason 等截断信号，再考虑是否修复 JSON。

title: I wanted to know which project was eating my Claude Code quota
content:
When I hit my Claude Code 5-hour or weekly limit, I want to know which project used it up. /usage doesn't answer that. It gives account-wide percentages plus a few tags like ">150k context" or "4+ parallel sessions". Nothing is broken down per project, and I can't check those percentages against anything. Claude Code already writes per-message token usage into every local session transcript under ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl . So I wrote a plugin, quota-audit, that reads those files and breaks the usage down per project and per skill. It also shows the exact times a rate limit was hit and which repo was blocked. Everything stays on your machine. It only reads those files and sends nothing anywhere. What the report looks like It opens with a few computed findings. After that comes one overview row per window (5h, 24h, 7d), then detail for the longest window. Here's a trimmed example: KEY FINDINGS (7d window)
  • Estimated cost $147.31, 65% of it in my-app ($95.20)
  • Top skill is ai-wo
author: Rosehsu
summary_zh: 作者发现 Claude Code 的 /usage 命令只提供账户级别的用量百分比，无法按项目拆分，于是开发了 quota-audit 插件，直接读取 ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl 本地会话记录中的逐条消息 token 用量，按项目和 skill 统计配额消耗。插件还能显示触发速率限制的具体时间和被阻塞的仓库，全部在本地运行、不上传数据，适合想排查 5 小时/周配额去向的重度用户。

title: Fast Models, Slow Evidence: A Paired and Self-Audited Evaluation of System-1 Decision Models for LLM Agent Harnesses
content:
arXiv:2610.02267v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agent harnesses make many small, typed decisions per task: which model to call, which tool to use, whether retrieved text is relevant, whether an input carries an injection. System-1 decision models answer such questions in a single forward pass with class probabilities, promising large cost and latency savings over LLM calls. We present a paired evaluation of an open-weight (Laya) and a hosted (Jev) System-1 model on 11 agent decision points built from 18 public sources: 7,283 base cases plus 6,640 robustness variants, with byte-identical inputs, paired tests, and cross-hardware and cross-day reproducibility checks. Jev is significantly more accurate on 9 of 11 decision points (+10.8 to +46.0 pp). Neither model beats chance on zero-shot model routing, and they tie on RAG relevance gating. Laya changes 30% of its answers when the option order is reversed and degrades sharply with many or similar candidates (31% at 50 nearest-neighbour to
author: Jiawei Li
summary_zh: 论文对 LLM Agent harness 中用于快速决策的 System-1 模型做了配对评估。这类模型一次前向传播即可完成模型路由、工具选择、检索相关性判断和提示注入检测，能替代部分 LLM 调用来降低成本和延迟。研究对比了开源的 Laya 和托管的 Jev 两个模型，覆盖 11 个决策点、7,283 个基础用例和 6,640 个鲁棒性变体，并做了跨硬件、跨日期的复现检验。结果显示 Jev 在 9 个决策点上明显更准，两者在零样本设置下均未超过随机水平，说明在 Agent 工作流中用小模型替代 LLM 做决策时需要谨慎验证。

title: Quoting Felix Rieseberg
content: The "old" version of Cowork runs model inference in the cloud, executing tool calls in an Anthropic-provided VM we shipped to your computer. We added the VM for capability, safety, and security reasons - mapping in just the data you explicitly added to your session. People loved what they were able to do with Claude but didn't love the disk, battery, and performance cost of running the VM locally. Also, people didn't love that closing your laptop means the work stops. The "new" version of Cowork runs model inference and the VM in the cloud. Each session gets its own sandbox, not sharing state with other sessions. When the VM needs something on the users' device (like a file), the desktop app is responsible for that file access tool call. [...] We think this solves a lot of problems we've heard about  (like using Cowork from a phone, keeping work running, or getting all the same power without losing battery to the VM) — Felix Rieseberg , Anthropic, see also this help page Tags: claude-c
summary_zh: Anthropic 的 Felix Rieseberg 讲了 Cowork 的架构调整：旧版在用户电脑上运行 Anthropic 提供的本地 VM 来执行工具调用，占用磁盘和电量、拖慢性能，而且合上笔记本任务就会停。新版把模型推理和 VM 都放到云端，每个会话有独立沙箱，需要访问本地文件时由桌面应用负责执行相应的工具调用。这篇内容讲清楚了 Claude 智能体产品在本地与云端执行、安全隔离和使用体验之间怎么取舍。

title: pwasm 0.2a0
content: Release: pwasm 0.2a0 pwasm is one of my folly projects - an entirely vibe-coded pure Python WebAssembly engine that I built in January during my first bout of AI mania . I hadn't touched it since January, so I decided to let Claude Opus 5.5 loose on it and see if it could make any significant improvements: Evaluate current state of pwasm - then consider what it would take to get the MicroPython and micro JavaScript experiments from the research repo working under it - and what it would take to speed it up 42 commits later (with minimal follow-up prompting) it now handles almost all of the WASM specification, and the wheel from PyPI bundles working WASM builds of MicroPython , QuickJS and Micro QuickJS . I wouldn't trust this thing at all - hence the alpha version tag - but it's interesting seeing how today's models can improve on the work of models from 10 months ago. Tags: python , webassembly , vibe-coding
summary_zh: Simon Willison 用 Claude Opus 5.5 改进他此前完全靠 vibe coding 写出的纯 Python WebAssembly 引擎 pwasm。他只给了一句较开放的评估和改进指令，几乎没有后续提示，模型就提交了 42 次，让引擎基本覆盖了 WASM 规范，还打包了能运行的 MicroPython、QuickJS 和 Micro QuickJS。这个案例说明新模型能自主、长时间地推进已有代码库，但作者也提醒这类产物还不能直接信任。

title: Reflection AI's Beam: Why 23B Active Parameters Matter More Than 501B
content: Reflection AI just introduced Beam , its first open-weight model. The headline number is 501 billion parameters. The number builders should actually care about is 23 billion . What was announced (Oct 5, 2026) Architecture: a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501B total parameters and about 23B active per token, built for coding, reasoning, and agentic work. Pretraining: 23.8 trillion curated tokens, trained in under four weeks on a GB300 NVL72 cluster. Reinforcement learning at scale: 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs for four weeks, more than 100 million rollouts, about 1.3 billion sandboxes, and close to one million coding, agentic, and STEM environments. Context: midtraining extends effective context to 1M tokens. License and timing: early access now. Reflection says weights, a technical report, a model card, and fine-tuning tooling ship later this month under Apache 2.0 . Expected vs. actual Expected: a bigger open model means more hardware and a bigger bill for every answer. Actual
author: M.T.Ramkrushna
summary_zh: Reflection AI 发布首个开放权重模型 Beam。它采用稀疏 MoE 架构，总参数 501B，每个 token 激活约 23B，专为编程、推理和 Agent 任务设计。文章介绍了模型的训练规模：23.8T token 预训练，在约 1.3 亿沙箱、近百万个编程/Agent 环境中完成大规模强化学习，上下文可扩展到 1M。文章还指出，开发者更该关注激活参数量带来的推理成本和部署可行性。

title: The FP8 trap: my GPU bill dropped 47% because the model was printing "!!!!!!"
content: I had one hour on an AMD MI300X and one question: what does a token actually cost on it? One GPU, vLLM's ROCm build, Qwen2.5 at 7B, 32B and 72B. Thirty-two requests in flight, 256 output tokens max, priced at the $2.99/GPU-hr list rate. Every number below is wall-clock time × that rate ÷ tokens produced. The baselines came out clean. Four repeat checks of each untouched config, so I'd know how much the machine wobbles on its own: 7B: $0.227 per million output tokens 32B: $0.77 72B: $1.67 , on a single GPU, which still surprises me a bit The 72B repeats agreed to within 0.4%. That's a very quiet machine. The obvious next move FP8 halves the bytes per weight. vLLM will do it for you on load with one flag: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct --quantization fp8 Numbers: 32B: $0.77 → $0.449 (−41%) 72B: $1.67 → $0.872 (−47%) Three checks each, all well outside the noise. If I'd stopped there I would have written a very different post, and I'd have been telling you to cut your bill in half.
author: Throttle
summary_zh: 作者在单张 AMD MI300X 上用 vLLM ROCm 版测试了 Qwen2.5 7B/32B/72B 的单 token 推理成本。开启 FP8 量化后账单降了约 47%，但模型其实在输出「!!!!!!」这类无效内容。文章提醒大家，量化之后只看吞吐和成本会被误导，必须同时检查输出质量。

title: [query-inspector] A Claude Code skill for extracting and tuning SQL/ORM queries
content: query-inspector is a Claude Code skill that extracts the SQL/ORM queries from your project's source, then diagnoses and tunes missing indexes / N+1 problems / anti-patterns . Queries that run fine until the data piles up. N+1 problems that sail through code review. The real SQL your ORM generates, invisible in the code. It catches all of this right before you commit, not after it reaches production. Common pitfalls A query shipped without an index suddenly turns into a full scan once there are tens of thousands of rows. An N+1 problem slips through code review, and a single list API fires dozens of queries. You can't tell from the code alone what SQL JPA or QueryDSL will actually generate. Code review looks at logic, not "the queries this change will produce" from a SQL angle. QA rarely catches it either, because its test data is too small for a missing index or an N+1 to surface as a slowdown. These problems share one trait: they surface only after you ship. query-inspector moves that
author: 황용호
summary_zh: 介绍 query-inspector 这个 Claude Code Skill。它会从项目源码里抽取 SQL 和 ORM（如 JPA、QueryDSL）查询，在提交代码前诊断缺失索引、N+1 问题和常见反模式，并给出调优建议。它把数据量变大后才暴露的性能隐患提前到开发阶段发现，补上代码审查只看逻辑、不看实际生成 SQL 的盲区。

title: Claude Code on Pro, Max, Team or the API, and how to choose (October 2026 pricing)
content: Originally published at https://aicoding-guide.com . The first decision when adopting Claude Code is how you pay for it. There are two paths — a subscription (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) or API usage billing — and they differ in how cost works and how limits behave. The short answer: a subscription if you use it for hours most days, an API key if you drive it from CI and automation . The documentation puts enterprise averages at $150–250 per developer per month, and at that volume a subscription costs less. Every figure here was checked on the official pages on October 5, 2026 . Prices get revised, so confirm current numbers before you commit. Key point What you will learn Which plans include Claude Code, and which don't Subscription and API pricing, and how their limits differ The three options when you hit a limit, and which path fits your use The free plan does not include it The pricing page's comparison table lists Claude Code as "No" on Free . You need a paid plan or an API key.
author: aicoding-guide
summary_zh: 文章对比了 Claude Code 的订阅方案（Pro、Max、Team、Enterprise）和 API 按量计费，说明两者在成本结构和用量限制上的差别，所有价格均于 2026 年 10 月 5 日在官方页面核对过。结论是：每天高频使用数小时的人选订阅更划算，在 CI 或自动化流程中调用时用 API key 更合适。文中还引用官方数据，企业开发者人均月花费约 150–250 美元，在这个用量下订阅更便宜。

title: Choosing Before Acting: Comparative Value Estimation for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents
content:
arXiv:2610.02330v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) rely on long-horizon tool invocation sequences for complex tasks, where each invocation can alter the task state and condition subsequent decisions. In long-horizon tool use, final-outcome rewards provide weak credit assignment over long interaction traces. Step-level rewards can offer more targeted feedback, but obtaining reliable step supervision often requires human or LLM judgment, or additional rollouts to estimate the downstream effect of an intermediate decision. In this paper, we argue that effective tool-use agents should estimate the long-horizon value of a possible next tool invocation before executing it. This objective requires comparative supervision over alternative invocations under the same context, while logged trajectories only contain the invocation that was actually taken. Therefore, we propose Comparative Inference for Tool-use Agents (CITA). CITA trains a Comparative Inference Model (CI
author: Yu Li, Zheng Zhang, Xin Liu, Shengtian Yang, Guangfeng Cai, Lei Feng
summary_zh: 论文针对长链路工具调用智能体中仅靠最终结果奖励导致信用分配弱的问题，提出在执行前先对候选的下一步工具调用做比较式价值估计。核心思路是在同一上下文下，对多个备选调用进行比较监督，从而在不依赖大量人工或LLM标注、也不需要额外rollout的情况下获得更可靠的步级信号。这对构建和优化长任务Agent（如编程Agent）的决策质量有参考价值。

title: Decisions You Can Check: What solvi 1.0 Is For, and What It Will Not Do for You
content: solvi 1.0 is an open-source Python library for decisions you can check: fast solvers answer under a calibrated error promise, an LLM or a search takes the rest, a person decides what neither can, and every decision is hash-chained and replayable. It does not make a model smarter, and the article says where it lost. Read All
author: Maksim Kuznetsov
summary_zh: solvi 1.0 是一个开源 Python 库，用于构建可验证的决策流程：快速求解器在校准误差承诺内作答，其余交给 LLM 或搜索处理，两者都无法决定的交由人工裁决。所有决策都经过哈希链记录并可重放。文章坦承该工具不会让模型更聪明，也写明了它在哪些场景下表现不佳，对设计可审计的 LLM 工作流有参考价值。

title: Session discovery: conversations become unreachable, plus ghost and duplicate project entries
content: The public issue trackers of the major agent CLIs are the best place to read what "my agent forgot" actually looks like in the wild. One of the most detailed reports is titled, verbatim: Session discovery: conversations become unreachable, plus ghost and duplicate project entries The reporter works with roughly ten active conversations. The complaint is not that the model got weaker. It is that the conversations stopped being addressable: some of them cannot be opened at all, and the project list has grown ghost entries plus duplicates of the same project, so there is no obvious place to go back to. Two sibling reports describe the same class of failure from different angles: A feature request asks the CLI to suggest starting a new conversation when resuming a large or stale session, because resuming it drags in context that no longer describes the work. A second bug report asks for conversation-scoped visibility, so an agent serving one channel can recall sibling threads in that chann
author: qianqiuwanzi
summary_zh: 文章整理了主流 AI 编程代理 CLI 公开 issue 中关于会话发现的问题：用户的对话无法再打开，项目列表里还出现幽灵条目和重复条目。作者认为所谓「代理失忆」往往不是模型变弱，而是会话管理与恢复机制出了问题。文中还提到一个功能请求：在恢复过大或过旧的会话时，提示用户开新会话。这对理解长会话工作流的痛点有参考价值。

OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic […]

summary_zh: OpenAI 开始在 ChatGPT 和 Codex 的文本输出中加入一种看不见、可由机器识别的水印（textGrain），目前只对欧盟用户开放。OpenAI 称它的效果与 Google DeepMind 的 SynthID 相当或更好，而 Anthropic 8 月宣布的水印方案也基于 SynthID。这说明 AI 编程工具生成的内容会越来越容易被识别和追溯，使用 Codex 或 Claude 产出代码和文本的开发者需要留意合规问题。

title: Why I Don't Use AI to Remove PII Before Sending Data to AI
content: The author of the article is uncomfortable with AI-based redaction because the redaction model still needs to see the original data, which can compromise privacy. They propose a deterministic approach to PII detection and redaction, using validation and checksums to identify and remove sensitive information. Read All
author: Raviteja Nekkalapu
summary_zh: 作者指出用AI模型做PII脱敏存在悖论：脱敏模型本身仍需读取原始敏感数据，隐私风险并未消除。文章主张在把数据发送给LLM之前，采用基于校验规则和校验和的确定性方法识别并移除个人敏感信息，为LLM数据处理工作流提供了隐私保护思路。

title: How Are You Handling Vibe Coding Security?
content: Vibe coding may inadvertently ship vulnerabilities into production systems. Common vulnerabilities include hardcoded secrets and API keys, broken authorization, insecure defaults, and more. To address these issues, establish strict guardrails, integrate real-time security scanning, mandate human review for critical paths, and more. Read All
author: Zac Amos
summary_zh: 文章讨论 Vibe Coding（AI 辅助快速编程）可能把安全漏洞带进生产环境，常见问题包括硬编码密钥和 API Key、授权失效、不安全的默认配置等。作者建议的应对办法有：设立严格的护栏规则、接入实时安全扫描、关键路径必须人工审查。内容偏概述，可作为 AI 编程安全实践的入门参考。

title: Claude Max Plan Price 2026: Max 5x vs Max 20x, 5x Wins
content: The Claude Max plan price is $100 per month for Max 5x and $200 per month for Max 20x, both billed monthly only ( Anthropic Help Center ). Max 5x wins for most buyers: the two tiers are feature-identical, so the extra $100 buys nothing but headroom. Max 20x only pays off if you hit Pro-level limits every working day — and two separate Max 5x seats cost the same as one Max 20x, often the better split for two users. TL;DR Max 5x: $100/month. Max 20x: $200/month. Both figures from Anthropic's Help Center ; claude.com/pricing lists Max as "from $100 per month". The tiers differ in usage volume, not features. Max is everything in Pro plus 5x or 20x Pro usage, higher output limits, priority access at busy times, and early access to new features ( claude.com/pricing ). Max is monthly-only. Pro can be billed annually at $17/month ($200 up front) or $20/month; Max has no annual option and no standard discounts ( Anthropic Help Center ). Usage limits still apply on Max. Anthropic's pricing page
author: Shaam
summary_zh: 文章对比了 Claude Max 两档订阅（Max 5x 月费 100 美元，Max 20x 月费 200 美元）。两档功能完全相同，只是用量额度不同，所以作者认为大多数用户选 Max 5x 就够了；只有每个工作日都会用满 Pro 额度的重度用户才值得买 20x。两人使用时，买两个 Max 5x 账号往往比合用一个 20x 更划算。
